“Now the man Moses was very humble” … We can learn … “man” from the word “man,” but we cannot learn … “man” from … “the man,”

“Now the man Moses was very humble” (Numbers 12:3). The Gemara answers: We can learn a verbal analogy to the word “man” from the word “man,” but we cannot learn a verbal analogy to the word “man” from the phrase “the man,”

p: the attribute of goodness or the attribute of retribution?
One must say the attribute of goodness … than the attribute of retribution. … With regard to the attribute of retribution, … states:
One must say the attribute of goodness is greater than the attribute of retribution. With regard to the attribute of retribution, in the case of the Flood, the verse states:
“And the windows of heaven were opened” … with regard to the attribute of goodness, … states:
“And the windows of heaven were opened” (Genesis 7:11), which indicates that there were only windows. Whereas, with regard to the attribute of goodness, in the case of the manna, the verse states:
and opened the doors of heaven,
and rained down manna upon them to eat and gave them heavenly grain”
